priorConsentForm.description: The consent form this study relies on.

reb.label: Research ethics
reb.description: The Research Ethics Board reviews every study.

classification.description:
Work that is research going ahead as quality improvement, or a "retrospective" study that in fact contacts people or collects new data, which changes the consent obligation entirely.

Look at: the stated purpose against the protocol's methods; any contact or new collection.

Policy: TCPS 2 Art. 2.5 (p. 21); Ch. 5 §D (p. 87); Art. 5.6 (p. 90).

Consult QIRC when the answer is quality improvement, and Data Services to confirm the source systems.

design.description: Some designs are not a straightforward chart review, such as mixed methods with a chart review component, and need more than this form asks.

identifiability.description:
Whether the data is identifiable decides whether consent is required at all. Coded data treated as non-identifiable while the team can reach the key lets a study proceed without consent and without the waiver conditions ever being tested. Small cohorts, rare diagnoses and narrow geography make re-identification easier.

Policy: TCPS 2 Ch. 5 §A (pp. 79-80) and Glossary (pp. 271-272); Art. 5.5A, 5.5B; PHIPA; UHN Privacy and Access Policy 1.40.007.

Consult Data Services, who build the extract and can state key custody and the field list, and the Privacy Office when data arrives directly identifying.

waiver.description:
Every condition of a waiver is mandatory: a study approved on partial satisfaction is not approved. Use without a lawful basis exposes the institution and costs public trust.

Look at: whether each condition is argued, not just asserted; inconvenience alone is not a reason. Art. 3.7A does not apply to secondary use.

Policy: TCPS 2 Art. 5.5A (p. 88), six conditions; Art. 5.5B (p. 90); PHIPA s. 44.

Only the REB can grant a waiver.

authority.description:
Data released without the custodian's authorization, or used beyond the conditions the custodian attached. The REB cannot approve what the custodian has forbidden.

Policy: TCPS 2 Art. 5.5A(f) (pp. 88-89); PHIPA; UHN Privacy and Access Policy 1.40.007; data sharing agreement requirements.

Consult Data Services and the Privacy Office, and Legal when an external agreement is involved.

linkage.description:
Linking datasets can make identifiable what was not identifiable in either. Linkage needs approval before it is done: approval after the merge is not a remedy.

Look at: whether the safeguards are proportionate to how likely re-identification is, and how bad it would be, across collection, use, linkage, analysis, storage, sharing and dissemination.

Policy: TCPS 2 Art. 5.7 (pp. 91-92); Art. 2.4 (p. 19); Art. 5.3; PHIPA.

Consult Data Services, who perform the linkage, and the Privacy Office for an external dataset.

indigenous.text: First Nations, Inuit and Métis data governance
indigenous.description:
Secondary use of data identifiable as coming from an Indigenous community needs engagement before it begins. This is about community authority over data, not individual vulnerability. Geography alone can trigger it.

Policy: TCPS 2 Ch. 9, Art. 9.20-9.22 (pp. 179-180); OCAP principles; UHN Indigenous Health Policy.

Consult the Indigenous health and community partnership function.

sensitive.description:
Stigma, discrimination, and consequences for employment, insurance, immigration or legal status, which the applicant is often not the right person to recognize.

Policy: TCPS 2 Art. 5.5A (p. 89); Ch. 4 (p. 67); PHIPA; UHN Privacy and Access Policy 1.40.007.

transfer.description:
Health information going to a partner, a service provider, an automated or AI processing tool, or outside Canada, without that transfer being assessed. Applicants often don't see transcription, statistical consultants or document processing as a transfer at all. Destination and safeguard are what this turns on.

Policy: TCPS 2 Art. 5.3 (pp. 85-86), 5.4 (p. 87); PHIPA; UHN Information Security Policy 1.40.028; UHN Cloud Security Standard; PIA and TRA requirements.

Consult Digital (demand intake), the AI Hub for automated processing, the Privacy Office for a PIA and Security for a TRA.

safeguards.description:
A breach, unauthorized access, or no way to show proper handling on audit. Data kept without limit, or destroyed without a record.

Policy: TCPS 2 Art. 5.1-5.4; PHIPA; UHN Records Policy 1.30.007; UHN Information Security Policy 1.40.028.

Consult the Privacy Office for a PIA, Security for a TRA, and Records Management for any deviation from 1.30.007.

rigour.description:
Research waste and harm at the population level when the question, cohort or variables don't fit.

Look at: whether the inclusion and exclusion criteria suit the question; whether identifiable information is essential.

Policy: TCPS 2 Art. 4.1 (p. 67); Art. 2.7 (p. 21); Art. 5.5A(a) (p. 88).

equity.description:
Groups included or left out for reasons unrelated to the question, by language, age, race or ethnicity, sex or gender, which can perpetuate harm and bias the results.

Look at: whether the criteria could reproduce disparities in who takes part in research, and what that means for validity.

Policy: TCPS 2 Art. 4.1, 4.7.

Consult Research IDEA and IHP.

reporting.description:
People or small groups identifiable in published results, even from an aggregate analysis.

Policy: TCPS 2 Art. 5.3 (p. 86); Art. 5.2 (p. 84).

incidental.description:
A clinically actionable finding with no consent relationship to disclose it through, or a worrying pattern with no plan for what happens next.

Policy: TCPS 2 Art. 3.4 (p. 41); Art. 5.6 (p. 90).

Clinical services need to be involved where actionable findings are foreseeable.

terminology.description:
Terms used loosely can describe the methods inaccurately and mislead the review.

Policy: TCPS 2 Art. 6.11; Art. 2.7.

conflict.description:
Undue influence, compromised privacy or confidentiality, or bias in decisions that affect participants or the study's integrity.

Look at: whether the conflict is real, potential or perceived, and whether it could affect welfare or integrity.

Policy: TCPS 2 Art. 7.4; Art. 3.2(e).

dateRange.description:
A date range reaching into the recent past may use data beyond what the waiver was granted for: some of those people could still be asked.

Look at: whether the end date is far enough in the past; whether patients are still being seen.

Policy: TCPS 2 Ch. 1, Ch. 3.

ai.description:
Studies building AI tools, and studies using AI to carry out research, sharpen every risk above. TCPS 2 has not caught up, and guidance for REBs is thin.

Consult the AI Hub and Digital.

digitalReview.label: Digital review
digitalReview.description: UHN Digital reviews the software, services and data flows the study relies on.

hosted.text: UHN-hosted services and data staying internal
hosted.description:
Data exposure and cyber risk from the services the study runs on, and whether data stays within UHN.

An integration with an external tool needs a Digital Demand.

externalSoftware.description:
Software hosted outside UHN that patient data goes into. Academic sponsors' agreements need security language added; industry sponsors outside the large pharmaceutical companies list need a manual check.

Look at: the software and its license holder, and decide whether to approve.

data.description: Patient data, or data entered by participants, needs a Digital Demand.

network.description: Anything set up on the UHN network, and sponsor devices that need internet access.

reuse.description: A tool approved for another study may be used differently here: new features, workflow, transfers or access.

policy.description: Deviations from the policies on storage, transport and destruction need Privacy's view.

ai.description: Generative AI, NLP and other AI tools, and above all the study's data used to train or refine a model, which needs a Digital Demand and the AI Hub intake.

deptHead.label: Department head
deptHead.description: The head of the department or division confirms the study fits and can be supported.

awareness.description: What the department is taking on, and with whom.

standing.description: Look at: the investigator's appointment status, whether they are in good standing, and whether the study falls within their expertise and responsibilities.

resources.description: What the study needs from the department.

landscape.description: Overlapping studies, datasets and objectives, and chances to collaborate.

conflict.description: Whether a relationship management plan is in place and mitigations are documented.

cta.label: Agreements
cta.description: Clinical Trial Agreements reviews the agreements with any outside organization.

external.description: Who is involved from outside UHN, what flows where, and what agreements cover it.

lmp.label: Laboratory Medicine
lmp.description: The Laboratory Medicine Program confirms it can extract the data asked for.

extraction.text: Data availability and staff to pull it
extraction.description: Whether the divisions can provide what is asked, and when.

jdmi.label: Medical Imaging
jdmi.description: The Joint Department of Medical Imaging confirms it can provide the images asked for.

effort.description: How many images, which ones, how anonymized and by when.

privacy.description: How images are transferred, where they go and who sees them.

commercial.description: Any relationship between the investigator and an outside company.

crdac.label: Princess Margaret data
crdac.description: The Clinical Research Data Access Committee reviews uses of Princess Margaret oncology data.

use.text: Use and interpretation of oncology data
use.description: Appropriate use, interpretation and context of clinical oncology data, and collaboration with the disease site.

secondary.description: Data from an earlier trial or study at UHN.

rqi.label: Research quality
rqi.description: Research Quality and Integrity checks the principal investigator's training.

gcp.description: Good Clinical Practice training, and when it was completed.

healthProfessions.label: Health Professions
healthProfessions.description: Health Professions is made aware of studies involving health professionals. Acknowledging is enough.

reidentification.description: Health professionals taking part, and whether the data identifies them.
